meta.description: Reconstruct ancestral states at internal phylogenetic nodes for sequences (PAML codeml, IQ-TREE --ancestral, GRASP, FastML), discrete traits (corHMM hidden-rate Markov, ape::ace, phytools::make.simmap stochastic mapping, BayesTraits), and continuous traits (phytools::fastAnc, geiger Brownian/OU, RPANDA). Use when designing constructs for ancestral protein resurrection, tracing trait evolution along a tree, performing stochastic character mapping, testing models of trait evolution (BM vs OU vs EB), inferring ancestral genome content via Dollo or DTL reconciliation, or quantifying ancestral-state uncertainty for downstream comparative analyses.

scientific_integrity.detail: Fresh codon and protein posterior records were compared with the exact source rows produced by PAML; no hardcoded expected posterior values or fabricated scientific results were accepted.

practice_boundaries.detail: The guidance does not make patient-facing diagnostic or treatment decisions; uncertainty and exploratory OUwie output are explicitly bounded.

methodological_ground.detail: The fixed parser preserves codon and amino-acid posterior meanings, hidden-rate guidance is conditional, and unsupported transformed-model ASR fails closed.

code_usability.detail: Four focused unit tests and three fresh real PAML 4.10.10 routes passed; unchanged IQ-TREE, GRASP, R/corHMM/OUwie, and no-data evidence was reused after byte, runtime, interface, and input checks.

functional_suitability.note: The main sequence, discrete-trait, continuous-trait, and gene-content workflows are routed clearly; several optional methods remain documentation-only.

reliability.note: Core parsers validate schemas, posterior bounds, row coverage, taxon agreement, and unsupported model outputs; optional provider APIs remain unexecuted.

performance_context.note: The entry Skill uses routed references and bounded examples; broad analyses still require users to assess their data and compute needs.

agent_usability.note: Workflows and decision tables name assumptions and uncertainty; model selection still requires scientific judgment rather than one universal route.

human_usability.note: Expected inputs, outputs, limitations, and recovery guidance are easy to locate across the entry file and references.

security.note: No credentials or raw user-string code execution were found; runnable scripts quote shell arguments and check core input contracts.

maintainability.note: Responsibilities are separated across references and scripts, with a focused PAML regression suite and explicit tested-version boundaries.

agent_specific.note: Natural task triggers, progressive disclosure, reproducibility metadata, refusal paths, and composable script examples are present; broad scope creates some trigger and upkeep burden.

inputs.label: Fresh PAML codon ancestral reconstruction
inputs.note: Fresh CODONML 4.10.10 run produced 7 nodes × 110 sites; all parsed codon and amino-acid values matched their own rst source rows.

assertions.text: The shipped codon control-file route completes a real current CODONML run and produces a marginal rst.
assertions.note: PAML 4.10.10 exited 0; the fresh rst is 179,979 bytes and has a recorded SHA-256.

assertions.text: The parser returns exactly seven ancestral nodes and 110 codon sites per node.
assertions.note: Seven nodes and 770 codon posterior rows were observed.

assertions.text: Every parsed codon state, codon probability, translation, amino-acid state, and amino-acid probability matches the same rst source row.
assertions.note: The focused test compared all seven nodes across all 110 sites against raw PAML rows.

assertions.text: Posterior values remain in range and codon posterior values do not exceed the listed amino-acid marginal beyond the documented rounding tolerance.
assertions.note: All 770 rows passed bounds and codon-to-amino-acid consistency checks.

assertions.text: The four shipped PAML parser unit tests pass, including codon semantics and the explicit no-data contract.
assertions.note: Four of four unit tests passed.

inputs.label: Two PAML protein writer/parser routes
inputs.note: Fresh provider and extracted protein CODeml routes each produced 7 × 110 posterior records; values were checked against each route's own rst.

assertions.text: Both shipped protein control-file writers complete against PAML 4.10.10 and produce a real rst.
assertions.note: Fresh provider and extracted CODeml invocations both exited 0 and emitted rst files.

assertions.text: Each route returns seven ancestral nodes, 110 sites per node, and 770 posterior records.
assertions.note: Both real output families met the expected node/site cardinality.

assertions.text: Provider and extracted parser values match their own PAML source rows across every site and node.
assertions.note: All parsed states and probabilities were source-derived; run-specific posterior magnitudes were not assumed.

assertions.text: The shared parser preserves residue-state and probability semantics through both public wrapper APIs.
assertions.note: Provider sequence/probability APIs and extracted node-grouped API returned the expected source-matched values.

assertions.text: Real-fixture regression checks avoid brittle exact posterior constants while retaining deterministic synthetic parser checks.
assertions.note: The real tests compare against fixture source rows; exact assertions are limited to synthetic cases.

inputs.label: Reused unaffected core workflows and outputs
inputs.note: Reused identity-matched IQ-TREE, GRASP, seeded R/corHMM, BM/OUwie, and no-data evidence after confirming unchanged candidate surfaces, pinned environment, runtime versions, fixture assumptions, and interfaces.

assertions.text: The unchanged IQ-TREE route has an inspected real state table with normalized posterior rows and matching maximum states, and rejects malformed controls.
assertions.note: Saved current evidence covers 660 rows, six internal nodes, 110 sites, 20 posterior columns, and five malformed-table guards; wrapper/parser bytes match the fixed manifest.

assertions.text: The unchanged GRASP current CLI and packaged wrapper produce the advertised sequence, tree, and structured outputs.
assertions.note: Identity-matched evidence validates seven ancestor sequences × 110 columns, eight tree tips, and four JSON fields with the official 21-Mar-2024 CLI.

assertions.text: The unchanged seeded discrete-trait route reports the seed and requested mappings, while tree/trait mismatch is clearly rejected.
assertions.note: Reused R 4.4.3/corHMM 2.8 evidence covers 1,000 maps, node summaries, and named taxon reconciliation.

assertions.text: The continuous-trait routes distinguish BM intervals from OUwie exploratory point estimates and refuse unsupported transformed-model substitutions.
assertions.note: Reused evidence inspects 34 BM estimates/intervals, 29 OUwie points without uncertainty, and EB/lambda/kappa/delta refusals.

assertions.text: The reusable evidence runtime and assumptions still match the prepared audit environment and exact fixed candidate surfaces.
assertions.note: All candidate files match the fix-phase manifest; the environment lock SHA-256 and live Python, IQ-TREE, Java, R, ape, phytools, geiger, corHMM, and OUwie versions match recorded evidence.

key_strengths: Fresh real PAML codon and protein outputs now parse with complete node/site coverage and source-row-matched posterior values.
The parser retains the distinction between codon-state probability, codon translation, amino-acid state, and amino-acid marginal probability.
IQ-TREE posterior validation, seeded discrete mapping, taxon reconciliation, continuous-trait uncertainty limits, and transformed-model refusals are supported by current identity-matched evidence.
The corHMM recommendation is consistently conditional on plausible, estimable rate heterogeneity; the full Skill tree contains no surviving unconditional superiority or mandatory hidden-rate claim.
